text:
maya: quick heads up — nightly autotune showed a latency regression on the sm86->sm90 pool. seqlen=256, bursty traffic: p50 up ~10%, p95 up ~14%. KV cache hit rate dropped in the same run. attaching short excerpt below.

maya: microbench run summary:
```
model: small-llm
seq: 256
batch: variable (burst mean 6)
kernel-selection: auto
old: p50=82ms p95=210ms kv_hit=98%
new: p50=90ms p95=240ms kv_hit=87%
```

samir: wow kv_hit down to 87% — looks like more cache invalidations or we hit a different KV path.

dmitri: can you paste the probe output? specifically the arch capability detection (SM, TC, BF16, FP8) — suspect kernel pick changed.

maya: here: `arch_probe --device=sm86` output snippet:
```
SM=8.6
tensor_cores=true
bf16=true
fp8=maybe
cap_flags=0x1a3
selected_kernel=matmul_tc_prefetch
```

hana: hm `fp8=maybe` is suspicious — we had a flaky driver report on the sm90 nodes last week that returned incomplete FP8 capability. If we optimistically pick TC/FP8 kernels they can serialize other paths and hurt KV cache locality.

dmitri: that matches — if the runtime chooses the TC-prefetch matmul on write paths, we might be evicting/moving KV lines differently. Also TC kernels sometimes enable different shared-memory tiling, which can change L2 behavior.

samir: are these nodes the ones that upgraded to driver 545.x? I remember a weird nvml quirk.

maya: yes, the pool was rotated after the infra update. I saw the driver version bump in metadata.

maya: short repro script I used (if you want to run locally):
```bash
# run a small bursty workload
perf/microbench --model small-llm --seq 256 --burst 60 --batch-mean 6 --kernel=auto --kv-profile=on
```

dmitri: immediate mitigation idea: change capability detection ordering to require a conservative double-check for FP8/TC support: probe driver + run 1 short microkernel that validates TC bf16 path throughput. If probe disagrees, prefer scalar matmul kernel for seqlen>=128.

hana: yes + also add a temporary runtime flag `runtime.force_tc_precise_check=true` so we can A/B via canary without rebuilding images.

samir: telemetry: we should record `kernel_variant_chosen`, `arch_probe_result`, and `kv_hit_rate` for the first 30s of a session. That will let us associate kernel flips with kv thrash.

ci-bot: perf job scheduled: https://ci.internal/perf/13072 (sm86/sm90/sm92 matrix, autotune+control) :eyes:

dmitri: I'll draft a small patch to arch_probe. Plan:
- add `tc_precise_check` which launches a 128-token microkernel (no kv) to verify performance characteristics
- prefer non-TC fastpath when seqlen > 128 unless `tc_precise_check` passes
- expose `runtime.flags.prefer_precise_tc_check` (default false)

maya: patch looks good in theory. can we make the microkernel cheap (like 5 warm tokens + 32 measure) so overhead is minimal)?

dmitri: yep target ~50ms overhead across tested GPUs. snippet for config we can flip at runtime:
```json
{
  "kernel_selection": "auto",
  "flags": {
    "prefer_precise_tc_check": "true",
    "seqlen_tc_threshold": "128"
  }
}
```

hana: also add a short-circuit: if KV hit rate in warmup < 95% then fall back to non-TC path for this session. That prevents repeated thrashers from staying on a bad path.

samir: agree. Also log a single sample of `sm_version/driver/build` when this decision is made.

maya: i'm going to roll a canary with `prefer_precise_tc_check=true` + `seqlen_tc_threshold=128` on pool-a (5 nodes) and monitor console metrics + kv hit rate. will revert quickly if p95 increases.

deploy-bot: Canary started for pool-a with flags: prefer_precise_tc_check=true seqlen_tc_threshold=128 — canary id perf-canary-2026-03-18-01

ci-bot: perf runs queued: job 13072 and job 13073 (control vs canary). expect results in ~45m.

dmitri: if perf confirms improvement, I'll push the patch and add the telemetry fields. We should also add a short note in the release notes about the conservative TC gating.

maya: thanks. next steps: 1) monitor canary dashboard 2) run localized repro on 2 dev nodes to validate 3) patch arch_probe and telemetry if CI looks good. ping me if you want me to run extra traces.

hana: :thumbsup: good plan. also file a follow-up to check driver 545.x quirk with infra.

samir: adding an issue for KV-thrash-observability so we don't lose context.

maya: resolving for now — will post perf links once CI done. :eyes:
